card.statement:
Consider $(1-w/z)^{-1}$ is considered as a formal series in $w/z$.

(1)

For a formal series $a(z)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb{Z}}a_{-d}z^{d}$, the coefficient of $z^{0}$ in $(1-w/z)^{-1}a(z)$ is $\sum_{d\geq 0}a_{-d}w^{d}$.

(2)

For a formal series $a_{-}(z)=\sum_{d\geq 0}a_{-d}z^{d}$, we have

$(1-w/z)^{-1}a_{-}(z)=(1-w/z)^{-1}a_{-}(w)+O(z).$

(3)

For a formal series $a_{+}(z)=\sum_{d\geq 0}a_{+d}z^{-d}$, we have

$(1-w/z)^{-1}a_{+}(z)=a_{0}+O(z).$

The proofs are straightforward, so we omit them.

3.3.2. The case $r=1$

As a demonstration, let us show

$\displaystyle\bigl((q/t)^{d-1}\eta_{d}+D_{d}\Delta_{h_{1}}\bigr)v_{n}^{(0)}=0\quad(d\geq 2)$

(3.29)

Hereafter we will use

$\eta_{+}(z):=\sum_{d\geq 0}\eta_{d}z^{-d},\qquad\eta_{-}(z):=\sum_{d\leq 0}\eta_{d}z^{-d}.$

We will also denote by the symbol $\equiv$ the equivalence of formal series up to $z^{-2}$ (ignoring $z^{-1},z^{0},z^{1},\ldots$ parts). Thus the relation(3.29) can be expressed as

$\displaystyle\bigl(t/q\cdot\eta_{+}(zt/q)+D(z)\Delta_{h_{1}}\bigr)v^{(0)}(w)\equiv 0.$

(3.30)

By (3.27) in Lemma 3.8 we have

$\displaystyle D(z)\eta(z_{1})v^{(0)}(w)=(1-w/z)(1-z_{1}/w)^{-1}f(z_{1}/z)v^{(0)}(w)\eta(z_{1})D(z).$

Thus as formal series in $\cal{F}$ we have

$\displaystyle D(z)\eta(z_{1})v^{(0)}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}=(1-w/z)(1-z_{1}/w)^{-1}f(z_{1}/z)v^{(0)}(w)\eta_{-}(z_{1})\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}.$

Taking coefficients of ${z_{1}}^{0}$ in both sides and using Lemma 3.9, we have

$\displaystyle D(z)\,\eta_{0}\,v^{(0)}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}$ $\displaystyle=(1-w/z)f(w/z)\cdot v^{(0)}(w)\eta_{-}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}$

$\displaystyle=\Bigl(-\dfrac{w}{z}+(q+t-1)t/q+\dfrac{(1-q)(1-t^{-1})t/q}{1-q/t\cdot w/z}\Bigr)\cdot v^{(0)}(w)\eta_{-}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}.$

$\displaystyle\equiv(1-q)(1-t^{-1})t/q\cdot(1-q/t\cdot w/z)^{-1}\cdot v^{(0)}(w)\eta_{-}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}.$

In the second line we used the formula

$(1-x)f(x)=-x+(q+t-1)t/q+\dfrac{(1-q)(1-t^{-1})t/q}{1-xq/t}.$

Now recall that by (2.23) we have $\Delta_{h_{1}}=\Delta_{e_{1}}=(1-\eta_{0})/\bigl((1-q)(1-t^{-1})\bigr)$. Using (3.27) we have

$\displaystyle D(z)\Delta_{h_{1}}v^{(0)}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}\equiv-t/q\cdot(1-q/t\cdot w/z)^{-1}\cdot v^{(0)}(w)\eta_{-}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}.$

(3.31)

On the other hand, by (3.28) in Lemma 3.8 we have

$\displaystyle\eta_{+}(zt/q)v^{(0)}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}$ $\displaystyle=(1-q/t\cdot w/z)^{-1}v^{(0)}(w)\eta_{-}(zt/q)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}$

$\displaystyle=(1-q/t\cdot w/z)^{-1}v^{(0)}(w)\eta_{-}(w)\cdot 1_{\cal{F}}.$

(3.32)

In the last line we used Lemma 3.9. Comparing (3.31) and (3.32), we have the desired formula (3.30).

3.3.3. Calculation of $D(z)\Delta_{h_{r}}v^{0}(w)$

We want to calculate $D(z)\Delta_{h_{r}}v^{0}(w)$, The difficult point is that we don’t have an explicit formula for $\Delta_{h_{r}}$. However we may use the explicit formula (2.4) for $\widehat{E}_{r}$ in Fact 2.4 and the translation formula between $e_{r}[s^{\lambda}]$ and $h_{r}[B_{\lambda}]$ in Lemma 2.5. Thus we start with $D(z)\widehat{E}_{r}v^{0}(w)$.
card.label: Lemma 3.9

paper.title: Whittaker vector of deformed Virasoro algebra and Macdonald symmetric functions
paper.abstract: We give a proof of Awata and Yamada's conjecture for the explicit formula of Whittaker vector of the deformed Virasoro algebra realized in the Fock space. The formula is expressed as a summation over Macdonald symmetric functions with factored coefficients. In the proof we fully use currents appearing in the Fock representation of Ding-Iohara-Miki quantum algebra. We also mention an interpretation of Whittaker vector in terms of the geometry of the Hilbert schemes of points on the affine plane.
